decision_points.question: How are dyads with a missing skin-tone rating handled?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a mutually-exclusive complete-case rule (drop if either rater missing, if both missing, if rater1 missing, or complete-case incl. IAT); an analyst applies one; none co-occur

decision_points.question: How is the skin-tone rating turned into the exposure variable for the primary analysis (continuous, dichotomized at which cutoff, or which categories/rows retained)?
decision_points.why_rival: median split, 0.25 cutoff, >=0.5 boundary, three-category keep-medium, drop-medium, endpoints-only, and continuous are alternative definitions of the same exposure — you can only define it once, and none of these co-occur

decision_points.question: What model specification estimates the adjusted skin-tone effect?
decision_points.why_rival: single-level logistic (robust SE / incl. referee bias), random-intercept-only, random-slope, three-level categorical, and two hierarchical structures are rival specifications of the one primary model; the 16/19 and 22/36 co-occurrences are model-comparison, not coexistence

decision_points.question: How is the estimated skin-tone effect converted into a reported quantity?
decision_points.why_rival: percentile risk contrast, extreme-value risk difference, Bayesian posterior probability, and extracted average marginal effect are rival expressions of the same effect magnitude

decision_points.question: How finely is skin tone aggregated for the descriptive red-card-rate plot?
decision_points.why_rival: quintiles, 8 bins, 10 equal-width bins, or one point per distinct value are alternative granularities for the same rate visualization

decision_points.question: What minimum observation count must a skin-tone bin/value have to be plotted?
decision_points.why_rival: a >=50 vs >=100 support threshold for including a bin — one threshold is chosen

decision_points.question: How is the bivariate skin-tone/red-card association tested?
decision_points.why_rival: a 2x2 chi-square vs a group-by-outcome chi-square of independence are rival setups of the same significance test

decision_points.question: How is the crude (unadjusted) skin-tone effect size reported?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option answering how the raw dark:light effect magnitude is expressed

decision_points.question: Is a cutoff reference line drawn on the skin-tone histogram?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option about annotating the exposure histogram

decision_points.question: Which skin-tone level is coded as the positive class for the binary exposure?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option fixing the direction/reference of the dichotomized exposure coding

decision_points.question: How is covariate balance across skin-tone groups examined?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option cross-tabulating covariates against skin-tone group

decision_points.question: How are predictors entered into the regression (single block vs hierarchical blocks)?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option specifying blockwise predictor entry order

decision_points.question: What sensitivity check on the exposure encoding is run?
decision_points.why_rival: explicitly a robustness refit (continuous instead of binarized), a separate decision from the primary exposure choice

decision_points.question: How much skin-tone data is missing (magnitude for the selection-bias check)?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option quantifying the amount of missingness

decision_points.question: How are potential confounders screened for association with skin tone?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option testing a player-level variable's association with the exposure

decision_points.question: How are unadjusted red-card rates by skin-tone group displayed with uncertainty?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option plotting grouped rates with Wald error bars

decision_points.question: Is skin-tone-rating missingness tested for association with the outcome?
decision_points.why_rival: sole option testing whether missingness is informative about the red card

decision_points.question: Is a cross-level skin-tone x referee-covariate interaction added on a plain random-intercept model?
decision_points.why_rival: distinct interaction extension on a different (plain random-intercept) base; co-occurs only with random-effects exploration, not with the country-bias interactions

decision_points.question: Is the skin-tone slope allowed to vary and be linked to a country-level bias score?
decision_points.why_rival: adds a random skin-tone slope tied to country bias; co-occurs with (can coexist alongside) the IAT and explicit-bias interactions, so it is its own component decision

decision_points.question: Is an implicit-bias (country-mean IAT) cross-level interaction added to the preferred model?
decision_points.why_rival: a yes/no moderator addition that co-occurs with the explicit-bias term — both can sit in one model, so it is a separate decision from 44

decision_points.question: Is an explicit-bias (country-mean Exp) cross-level interaction added to the preferred model?
decision_points.why_rival: a yes/no moderator addition that coexists with the IAT interaction (34/38/44 all co-occur in one run), marking it a complementary component rather than a rival of 38
